title: A Simple Tablet for Video Calls With Family: iPad, Fire HD 8 or Galaxy Tab A9+
subtitle: Three tablets worth a look, and the questions to ask about calling apps, prices and extras before you buy.
excerpt: A tablet can turn a small-screen phone call into an easier chat with the grandkids. Here is what we can confirm about the iPad, Amazon Fire HD 8 and Samsung Galaxy Tab A9+, and the one question to ask before you buy.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: Phone video calls work, but the picture is small. Holding a phone up for a long chat can get tiring, and it is hard to see a new baby's face or a grandchild's school project on a screen that size.

A tablet is a bigger, flat touchscreen, so it can make those calls easier to see. The trick is picking one that runs the same calling app your family already uses, and knowing what it costs once you add the extras.
How Video Calling on a Tablet Works

To make a video call, you open an app, tap a name, and the other person answers on their own phone, tablet or computer. The tablet needs a camera facing you, plus a way to get online. Both people generally need the same app.

Here is what the makers and retailers say about the cameras. Apple lists a 12MP Center Stage front camera on the iPad and says it keeps you in frame on a FaceTime call. Best Buy's AI-generated question-and-answer section says the Fire HD 8 has a front-facing camera and can make video calls, but that is not a formal spec, so confirm it before buying. The Samsung page we read did not give camera details, so check those on Samsung's buy page.

The calling app is where the choice matters most. FaceTime, Apple's calling app, works only on Apple devices. Amazon's Fire tablets run Fire OS, Amazon's own software, and get apps from the Amazon Appstore rather than Google Play. If your family uses Zoom, WhatsApp or Google Meet, check that the app is available on a Fire tablet before you buy. We did not confirm app availability for the iPad or the Galaxy Tab A9+, so check those as well.

A tablet needs an internet connection. Wi-Fi-only models need home Wi-Fi to work. Apple lists cellular iPad models too, and those need a data plan. We did not research those plans, so ask the carrier about cost.

A tablet is also not a safety device, and it is not a monitored alert service. And if touchscreens and passwords are hard for the person you are shopping for, a tablet may not suit them. A smart display or a simplified phone may be a better fit.

items: The right app: Ask your family which calling app they use, then confirm it is available on the tablet before you buy.
The real price: Some advertised prices depend on trading in an old device. Look for the price without a trade-in so you can compare fairly.
Extras that add up: Cases and covers cost extra. The Fire HD 8 cover, for example, is $32.99 at Best Buy (October 2026). Samsung says it offers a free book cover with purchase.
Camera details: Check that the model has a front camera, and look for the spec on the maker's page rather than relying on a store's automated answers.
Wi-Fi or cellular: Wi-Fi-only models need home Wi-Fi. Cellular models need a data plan.
Returns and setup help: Check the seller's return policy, and ask whether the store offers help getting started.

sections.content: If you are buying for a parent, it helps to sort out the basics before the tablet changes hands. Confirm the calling app is available, check the full price including any case, and make sure there is home Wi-Fi where the tablet will be used.
Prices matter here. A retailer listing we could not confirm suggests the iPad costs several times what a Fire HD 8 does, so compare current prices on the maker or seller pages before you decide.

Samsung's advertised starting price for the Galaxy Tab A9+ assumes you trade in an eligible device. Without a trade-in, you will pay more, so check the full price on the buy page before you compare it with the others. The same goes for any deal labeled "with trade-in."
sections.label: Before You Buy

sections.content: The best tablet for video calls is simply the one that lets your family see each other with the least fuss. Start with the app everyone already uses, check the full price, and take your time. Then pour a cup of coffee and say hello.

products.name: iPad 11-inch (A16)
products.blurb: Suits families who use FaceTime, which works only on Apple devices. It has an 11-inch screen and a 12MP front camera with Center Stage, which Apple says keeps you in frame during a FaceTime call.

products.name: Fire HD 8 (2024 release), 32GB
products.blurb: An 8-inch tablet sold at Best Buy. Best Buy's AI-generated Q&A says it has a front camera and can make video calls, but it runs Fire OS with the Amazon Appstore, so confirm your family's calling app is available first.

products.name: Galaxy Tab A9+
products.price: From $129.99 with eligible trade-in (Samsung, October 2026); higher without a trade-in
products.blurb: Samsung's page describes a larger screen and mentions a Samsung Kids mode. Screen size and camera details were not confirmed, so check them on the buy page; Samsung lists a free book cover with purchase.
